sections.title: The Birth of the Ruler from Bethlehem
observations: Micah prophesies the birthplace of the future ruler of Israel, emphasizing Bethlehem's significance despite its small size.
This prophecy points to the coming of Jesus Christ, who is born in Bethlehem, fulfilling this ancient prediction.
The mention of a ruler coming from Bethlehem highlights God's sovereignty in choosing the least likely places for His purposes.

sections.title: The Remnant of Israel
observations: Micah speaks of the remnant of Israel, indicating that not all will be lost, but a faithful group will remain.
This remnant will be protected and will rise to lead the people, showcasing God's faithfulness to His covenant.
The imagery of the shepherd suggests care and guidance, reflecting God's role as the ultimate shepherd of His people.

sections.title: The Judgment on Israel's Enemies
observations: The chapter concludes with a promise of judgment against Israel's enemies, emphasizing God's justice.
Micah reassures the people that God will not only protect them but also bring about justice against those who oppress them.
This serves as a reminder of God's power and the hope that He will ultimately vindicate His people.

importantVerses.commentary: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times.
He will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God.

questions: What does Micah's prophecy about Bethlehem reveal about God's plan for redemption?
How does the concept of the remnant encourage believers today?
In what ways can we see God's justice at work in our lives and in the world around us?
